report_types.name: SOC 2 Type 1
opinion_covers: Fairness of the description of the system as of a specified date
Suitability of the design of controls as of that date
report_types.typical_use: First-time reporting, newly implemented control environments, or a customer commitment that must be met before a Type 2 period can elapse.

report_types.name: SOC 2 Type 2
opinion_covers: Fairness of the description of the system throughout a period
Suitability of the design of controls
Operating effectiveness of controls throughout the period
report_types.typical_period_note: Periods are commonly 3 to 12 months. No specific minimum period is prescribed by the trust services criteria; period length is an engagement decision and user entities frequently expect 12 months for a mature program.
report_types.typical_use: Ongoing assurance to customers and prospects; the report most enterprise procurement teams request.

report_types.name: SOC 3
opinion_covers: Effectiveness of controls relevant to the selected trust services categories
report_types.typical_use: A general-use summary report suitable for public posting. Contains no detailed description of tests or results.
report_types.relationship_to_soc2: Derived from a SOC 2 Type 2 examination; not a substitute for it.

report_types.name: SOC 1
opinion_covers: Controls relevant to user entities' internal control over financial reporting (ICFR)
report_types.typical_use: Included for disambiguation only. SOC 1 uses control objectives defined by management, not the trust services criteria, and is out of scope for DriftGuard's SOC 2 knowledge layer.

disambiguation_rules: 'SOC 2 certification' is not a valid term. A SOC 2 engagement produces an attestation report containing a practitioner's opinion, not a certificate. DriftGuard must use 'report', 'examination', or 'attestation'.
A SOC 2 report is not 'passed' or 'failed'. The auditor issues an unqualified, qualified, adverse, or disclaimer opinion.
SOC 2 and SOC 1 are not interchangeable; scope, criteria, and intended users differ.
